renderingHints.currentPaddingBehavior: In the current ToolJet renderer, styles.padding values "default" and "none" do not add a visible content inset. Do not rely on this property to create card padding.
renderingHints.compactSideAlignment: The persisted defaults alignment="side", autoLabelWidth=false, and labelWidth=33 reserve one third of a wide component for labels and look broken. For a native horizontal details panel, set styles.autoLabelWidth.value="{{true}}" so the value column starts after the longest label.
renderingHints.approximateStaticHeight: Rows occupy about 38px plus a 12px gap. For N read-only fields, start near 50*N-12px rather than stretching the component; browser-verify wrapping and date/JSON fields.
renderingHints.polishedReadOnlyAlternative: For a display-only details card that needs reliable inset, spacing, and responsive columns, prefer one Html component with an explicitly projected binding and root CSS padding/box-sizing instead of KeyValuePair.

dataProjection.rule: An explicit fields array does not suppress undeclared keys from data; ToolJet appends those keys as visible rows. Bind data to a new object containing only intended field keys.
dataProjection.updateRule: Keep the complete fields array and the projected data object keyed identically. Object spreads are not safe projections.
dataProjection.defaultFieldRule: When explicit fields are authored, MCP populates fieldDeletionHistory to suppress ToolJet catalog demo fields that would otherwise be appended or positionally merged into custom field definitions.

detailPanelLayout.nativeSideRule: Never accept the persisted side-alignment defaults for a wide details panel. Set styles.autoLabelWidth.value="{{true}}"; fixed autoLabelWidth=false with labelWidth=33 creates an oversized empty label column.
detailPanelLayout.paddingCaveat: In the current renderer, styles.padding default/none does not create a content inset. Use the native component only when that edge treatment is acceptable and browser-verified.
detailPanelLayout.readOnlyAlternative: For a polished read-only details card, prefer Html with a freshly projected object and explicit root padding, gap, and box-sizing. Keep KeyValuePair when native field editing/changeSet behavior is required.

exposedVariables.name: selectedRecord
exposedVariables.semantics: Exposed values keyed by repeated child component name; this is not the original source listItem row.

exposedVariables.name: selectedRow
exposedVariables.semantics: Alias of selectedRecord; exposed values keyed by repeated child component name.

modes.gridViewRule: There is no separate GridView component type. Create type:"Listview" with mode:"grid"; GridView is only a get_component_catalog lookup alias.

repeatedChildren.atomicBatchRule: Create the Listview and every child that reads listItem in the same add_components call using client_ref/parent_ref. A listItem-bound child added later under an existing Listview can mount with empty exposed values.
repeatedChildren.localCanvasRule: Every repeated item, including every grid-mode cell, gives its children a fresh 43-column local canvas. A full-row child is left:0,width:43 even when the parent Listview renders several grid columns; do not divide child coordinates by the parent column count. Use smaller widths only to compose multiple children side by side inside one item.
repeatedChildren.htmlSizingRule: For an Html child, make the root element height:100% and box-sizing:border-box. Do not repeat the authored component height as a fixed px CSS height; wrapper chrome can make the inner canvas shorter and create a scrollbar in every item.
repeatedChildren.actionCompositionRule: When a native Button follows an Html card inside each repeated item, keep them visually contiguous (shared surface/border treatment and no arbitrary vertical gap) and set rowHeight to at least the lowest child bottom plus about 10px. A detached button reads as a separate record and an undersized row clips it.

selection.selectedRecordShape: Object keyed by repeated child component name. Each value is that child instance's exposed-variable object (for example selectedRecord.cardHtml.rawHTML); it is not the original listItem source row.
selection.sourceRowRule: If an action needs source-row fields, expose them through a repeated child or store the source row explicitly; do not assume components.<listview>.selectedRecord.<sourceField>.
aliases: selectedRow is the same child-exposed-value map
selectedRowId is the same index as selectedRecordId
selection.paginationCaveat: selectedRecordId/selectedRowId are rendered-item indexes and can be page-local when pagination is enabled; do not use them as durable record ids.

authoringHints.providerSetup: Map.jsx loads Google Maps using deployment public_config.GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY. If Google reports a configuration/access error, report the dependency and ask the deployment owner to fix it; do not invent a working key, suppress the warning, or claim the map is production-ready.
authoringHints.markerSelection: Use defaultMarkers entries with lat, lng and a stable source-record id. onMarkerClick publishes that whole object as selectedMarker before handlers run. Capture the selected id into the same detail context used by list selection. Do not match solely by coordinates: different visits may share a property.
authoringHints.look: In an app built in ToolJet UI 2.0, prefer ShadMap: markers from rows, status-toned pins, groups for thousands of rows, a popup and selection, on open tiles that need no API key. Use this Map only when the app needs Google's map (places search, Google's own tiles) and the deployment sets GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY; then set styles.mapLook "shadcn" for the UI 2.0 frame (theme radius, hairline border, card surface). Without a key it shows 'Add a Google Maps API key to show this map'.

Bound to a messages query, map its rows: {{(queries.getMessages.data || []).filter(m => m.thread_id === variables.threadId).map(m => ({ message: m.body, type: m.sender === 'agent' ? 'message' : 'response', name: m.author, timestamp: m.sent_at, messageId: 'msg-' + m.id }))}}; a new value (another thread picked, the query refreshed) replaces the history. userName and userAvatar, respondentName and respondentAvatar name the two sides when a message has no name. Sending fires onMessageSent with the text in components.<chat>.lastMessage.message (lastMessage is the whole message object, so save .message, not lastMessage, in a text column). Wire onMessageSent to the save or AI query; on that query's success run the appendHistory action ({{ { message: <reply text>, type: 'response', name: <sender> } }}) or refresh the history query, with setResponseLoading true before and false after (a typing indicator), and setError on failure. A RunJS query can drive it in one place: await components.<chat>.setResponseLoading(true); await queries.save.run(); await components.<chat>.appendHistory({ message, type: 'response' }); await components.<chat>.setResponseLoading(false). loadingHistory shows the history loading, disableInput blocks sending (with emptyText and placeholder saying why, such as before a check-in is done). Replies render markdown (lists, bold, tables); the user's own turns are plain text. Set chatTitle '' and both header buttons off (enableClearHistoryButton, enableDownloadHistoryButton) when a card title already names it, or the header is an empty band. authoringHints.styles: Every style falls back to the app theme, so set only what the design needs to blend in (its accent, surfaces, borders and text colours), taking colours from the app theme or brand, never the defaults of another product. Radii and sizes are px. Styles are the way to restyle a pack widget: a cssClass only takes effect with workspace Custom styles, and Tailwind class names the pack does not already use are not compiled, so do not rely on either; for a one-off visual a style cannot express, use an Html component. Bind loadingState to the query's isLoading (each widget draws a skeleton or spinner in its own shape); tooltip shows on hover.
authoringHints.validation: Top-level validation (not properties), each key as {value}: mandatory ("{{true}}": a value must be picked, or the checkbox checked) and customRule. customRule fails when it resolves to a non-empty string, which becomes the message: {{components.<name>.value.includes("@") ? "" : "Enter an email"}}. The message shows under the control after the user leaves it or a surrounding Form tries to submit; components.<name>.isValid and isMandatory are exposed, so gate a submit button with disabledState on them.
